tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For precise panel scribing, use RB Productions tools. First, lightly score the panel lines with a pencil to avoid deep scratches. Then, use the RB Productions Scriber to carefully trace along the lines, applying light pressure. For deep scribing, use the RB Productions Deep Scriber, but be cautious not to dig too deep. Finish with a gentle touch of a file or sandpaper to remove any burrs.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Compressed Air
tips.text: Regularly clean your Iwata airbrush needle to maintain performance. After each use, disassemble the needle, and using compressed Iwata air, blow through it to remove any dried paint. Then, use an Iwata Airbrush Cleaning Brush to scrub the needle's tip, followed by a quick blast of air to dry. Reassemble the needle, and you're ready for your next session.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs. Kabuki Tape
tips.text: For curved surfaces, use Tamiya Tape for easy application and removal. For complex shapes or tight spots, opt for Kabuki Tape's precision. Apply Tamiya Tape in long strips, using a ruler to crease sharp corners. For Kabuki Tape, cut it into smaller pieces, applying it carefully with tweezers. Both tapes can be left on overnight before painting without fear of peeling.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression with ICM Models
tips.text: ICM Models' sanding sticks come in varying grits for progressive sanding. Start with ICM 240 grit for heavy stock removal, then progress to ICM 320, 400, and 600 grit for refining. After each stage, wipe the part with a damp cloth to remove dust. For the finest details, use ICM 800 grit or higher, followed by a microfiber cloth for a mirror finish.

tips.title: Scratch-Building with Evergreen Styrene Sheet
tips.text: Evergreen Styrene Sheet is perfect for creating custom details or entire models. To cut parts, use a sharp hobby knife and a metal ruler for straight lines. For curves, use a self-healing cutting mat and a swivel knife. To bend styrene, carefully score the line with a needle tool, then use tweezers to bend along the score. Glue parts together using Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, allowing the solvent to do the work.
